_comment: CITABLE-ID NAMESPACE REGISTRY — the DEFINING FORM of every global citable-ID namespace (H / M / T / AR-WH-PL-CP / B / TECH_DEBT / PARITY / Class / D-C-F). Single-sourced DATA read by the Python resolver (tools/citable_ids.py) and, once it grows a consumer, by the foxtag C++ core and the nvim plugin's [REFERENCE] doc-viewer — the 'ONE RESOLVER, THREE CONSUMERS' shape D-390 specifies. TECH_DEBT-249 / D-389.
_encoding_law: ALL SCALARS ARE STRINGS — booleans included. The shared C++ reader (foxtag.hpp JVal) has Kind {STR, ARR, OBJ, OTHER} and NO bool/number kind, so a bare `true` parses as OTHER with an EMPTY string — a SILENT wrong-read, not an error. Measured 2026-07-19 with a compiled probe. tools/lib/toolio_schemas.json and corpus_contract.json both obey this. Do NOT 'clean this up' to native JSON types.
_why_NO_REGEXES: Deliberately declarative — anchor kind + literal prefix + flags — with ZERO regex syntax, and this is the load-bearing constraint rather than a style choice. `foxtag` contains no std::regex; it hand-parses char-by-char. D-393 pt 4 REFUTED a shared registry for the ref-index precisely because that one would have carried extraction REGEXES, which would CREATE parity risk instead of removing it. Every row here is expressible as: does the line start with X, is the ID bold, is there a Y after it. A hand-parser can honour that with startswith() and a digit scan. If a future namespace genuinely needs a regex, it does NOT belong in this file — give it a defining form a hand-parser can read, or keep it Python-side and say so.
_defining_form_not_mention: Every row anchors on the form that DECLARES an entry — a table row, a heading, a sentinel, a filename. NEVER a prose mention. A membership set built from mentions cannot go red: cite a nonexistent TECH_DEBT-999 in the same file that defines the set and it resolves. That is exactly why CI never saw the 8 dangling citations D-389 found (Class-51, in the resolver itself).

INVARIANT._use: Hard invariants H1..H22 — the CLAUDE.md table is the SSoT.
INVARIANT._why_bold_optional: H15/H18/H19/H21/H22 are BOLD rows; H1-H14 are not. A pattern requiring `|` immediately after the number silently dropped 6 of 22 — caught by checking the resolved count against the known H1..H22 range instead of trusting the match.
INVARIANT._why_citations_verifiable: SCOPE COLLISION. `H23` appears in prose as a PROPOSED-but-unwritten invariant and in audit synthesis text. Verifying bare `Hn` citations manufactures findings from forward-references.

META._use: Meta-disciplines M1..M10 — DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY § 11.5 is the SSoT.
META._why_bold_REQUIRED: LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic. DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY carries the § 11.5 DEFINING table (`| **M1 — …**`) AND a cross-reference index further down (`| M1 — … |`, plain). Treating bold as optional matched BOTH and reported 8 of 10 meta-disciplines as DOUBLE-DEFINED — every one a false positive. Shipping that would have made the guard's first run pure noise, which is the fastest way to get a guard ignored (M3).
META._why_citations_verifiable: SCOPE COLLISION, named verbatim in AR-14's false-positive surface: `M1`-`M9` are meta-disciplines globally but MEDIUM finding IDs inside audit reports.

TOOLCHAIN._use: Dev-plane toolchain invariants T1..T12 — the tools/CLAUDE.md T-index is the SSoT.
TOOLCHAIN._why_citations_verifiable: SCOPE COLLISION, MEASURED 2026-07-20: `T7-T18` are TEST ids in `test_v5_15_5_F4c_cfg_field_dispatch`, not toolchain invariants. Five of the guard's first-run 'dangling' findings (T13/T14/T15/T18/T19) were this.

ANTIPATTERN._use: Meta-anti-patterns AR-n / WH-n / PL-n / CP-n — the index table is the SSoT.
ANTIPATTERN._note: One doc owns FOUR namespaces, which is why it carries `owns_namespace: [AR, WH, PL, CP]` rather than a singular `registry_id:` — see doc-frontmatter-convention.md.

BLINDSPOT._use: Implementation-blindspot pillars B1..Bn — the taxonomy's headings are the SSoT.
BLINDSPOT._why_citations_verifiable: SCOPE COLLISION, named verbatim in AR-14: `B12`-`B17` are pillars globally but work-item IDs inside one synthesis doc.

TECH_DEBT._use: TECH_DEBT-n entries across the split ledger.
TECH_DEBT._why_id_body_stays_digits: `id_body: digits` is the FORWARD rule and stays that way. Exactly ONE grandfathered exception exists corpus-wide — TECH_DEBT-175a, minted by D-240 as a split of -175 — and the resolver accepts a single trailing ASCII lowercase letter so it resolves rather than silently collapsing onto its parent. D-409 CLOSED that form: a new split takes a fresh int id plus a `split_from:` field, because embedding the parent relationship INTO the identifier makes identity mutable, which is the same objection that killed the plane-qualified scheme (D-390). Do not read the suffix support as licence to mint -NNNb. The one instance cost four defects across two modules (a false defined-twice on -175, an unmatchable citation form, a 4295-byte block over-run, and an uncaught ValueError), which is the argument for the closure.
TECH_DEBT._why_int: Padding-insensitive: TECH_DEBT-005 and TECH_DEBT-5 are the SAME id, so normalising to int is what makes them resolve to one entry rather than two.
TECH_DEBT._hardened_2026_07_20: Was a by-MENTION scan (`TECH_DEBT-(\d+)` over raw ledger text). Measured at the flip: by-mention 248 vs by-defining 247 — the single dropped id is TECH_DEBT-101, which has NO defining row anywhere and is cited from ZERO engine sources, so nothing newly REDs. It is one of D-389's 8 dangling citations, i.e. the flip immediately surfaces a real defect the old set was structurally incapable of reporting.
TECH_DEBT._why_citations_verifiable: Distinctive multi-char prefix `TECH_DEBT-`; a bare mention cannot plausibly mean anything else.
TECH_DEBT._why_forwarding_tombstone_ok: The ledger's own rule (DOCS/tech-debt/open.md:22) sanctions leaving a 1-line forwarding tombstone in open.md when an entry MOVES to closed.md and cross-refs benefit. Such a heading is a POINTER, not a second definition — counting it as a defining site made TECH_DEBT-164, the ledger's single CORRECT example, appear as a split-brain collision. Discriminator is the entry FORMAT (a real entry declares `id:`; a pointer has no body), never a string match on 'CLOSED' or an arrow. Opt-in here because only the split TECH_DEBT ledger has this move-and-forward lifecycle; PARITY is a single file with no sub-files to forward between.

CLASS._use: Recurring-bug-pattern classes — the per-class FILENAME is the defining form.
CLASS._dropped_text_union: The predecessor ALSO unioned prose mentions of `Class N` from the catalog. Measured 2026-07-20: the union adds NOTHING (56 == 56) while making the set unable to go red. Dropped — a redundant leg that only costs falsifiability is strictly worse than no leg.
CLASS._why_citations_verifiable: SCOPE COLLISION: `Class 0` was matched out of a table describing the literal FORMAT `"Class <n>"`. Definition-side checks (double-definition, gaps) still apply; only CITATION resolution is skipped.

DECISION._why_two_sentinel_forms: MEASURED 2026-07-20 against the predecessor regex: 429 sentinels use `<!-- D/C/F:` and 19 use the shorter `<!-- D:`. A parser matching only the long form silently DROPPED 5 real ids including D-372..D-379 — the origin decisions of this very ship.
DECISION._why_id_exact: The id must be prefix+digits and NOTHING else. Taking everything between the delimiters over-accepted `DD-1`, `F-2-AMEND` and `P-1` as decision ids — junk that would then be reported as dangling citations forever. A resolver that admits malformed ids manufactures its own false findings.
DECISION._why_per_file: D-numbers RESTART per log, so the index is kept per-file and never unioned. A union would mask exactly the cross-log collision D-389 found — D-1..D-13 defined in TWO logs with genuinely opposite content (D-7 = ImGui stays vs hard-deprecated).
DECISION._why_citations_unverifiable: A bare `D-7` in prose cannot be resolved without knowing which log the citing doc means, and guessing would manufacture false positives at scale. Definition-side collisions ARE still reported (unambiguous); citation-side resolution is deliberately skipped rather than faked.
DECISION._why_supersede_exempt: TD-249's CONCRETE PARSE SPEC prescribes: flag a D-N defined in >=2 logs UNLESS the older carries `status: superseded`. The spec was written and recorded FIXED 2026-07-19; the exemption was never implemented, so 23 spec-exempt entries (D-1..D-13, C-1..C-4, F-1..F-6) were baselined as defects. That is 45% of the triage corpus unreachable by definition -- a guard that cannot converge is the guard that gets ignored (M3). Caught by the a-class adversarial review of the 0.2 handoff 2026-07-20.

_citation_verification_law: A namespace's CITATIONS are mechanically verified only when its id form is DISTINCTIVE enough that a bare mention cannot plausibly mean something else. Short letter+digit tokens (H23 / M8 / T13 / B16 / Class 7) collide with test ids, work-item ids, finding ids, section labels and forward-references to not-yet-written entries. AR-14's false-positive surface states this outright: scope overlap 'must NOT be mechanized — a checker cannot tell scopes apart; forcing it produces the noise that gets guards ignored.' The guard's FIRST run proved the point on itself: 8 of 18 'dangling citations' were scope collisions, and had they been baselined the ID-triage corpus would have started life half-noise. DEFINITION-side checks (double-definition, sequence-gap, reservation) are UNAFFECTED — those read the SSoT directly and carry no ambiguity.
_why_frozen_record_paths: A citation inside a FROZEN RECORD is not a claim about the present — it is a truthful artifact of what was true when written. A postmortem citing a then-real TECH_DEBT id is CORRECT, and 'fixing' it would rewrite history to satisfy a linter. The operator settled this scoping at D-390: 'for historical data thats no longer current i guess its not extremely critical' and 'a frozen record citing a then-real path is a truthful artifact; the guard's job is to stop the corpus getting WORSE, not to rewrite history.' So citations are resolved ONLY on LIVE surfaces — the current MASTER, in-flight plan bodies, the open/in-flight ledgers, ROADMAPs, decision logs, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN_SPECS. Measured 2026-07-20: of 10 dangling ids, 7 were cited exclusively from frozen records (a prior sprint's MASTER, a postmortem, May plan_checks, a superseded handoff) and 3 were genuinely LIVE. Flagging all 10 would have made the triage corpus 70% history-rewriting.
